About the Role:

Join Crusoe as an Engineering Manager to lead the Billing Platform team within our Cloud Customer Experience (CCX) organization. This is a highly cross-functional role at the intersection of engineering, product, and finance, responsible for building and operating the systems that power billing, payments, and cost transparency across Crusoe Cloud. You'll deliver a billing platform that is highly reliable, accurate, and scalable, while ensuring it is intuitive and transparent from a customer perspective. This a full-time opportunity for a leader with early management experience who thrives in ambiguous environments, enjoys aligning diverse stakeholders, and is passionate about building both strong teams and high-quality systems.


What You'll Be Working On:

  • Billing Platform Foundations: Lead development of core billing and payments infrastructure underpinning the Crusoe Cloud experience. Build systems for usage metering, pricing, invoicing, and payments, ensuring correctness, consistency, and auditability of financial data. Design scalable architectures supporting rapid product and pricing evolution.

  • Reliability & Trust: Establish billing as a highly reliable, trusted system for customers and internal teams. Define and uphold high standards for system uptime, accuracy, and data integrity, while building strong observability, reconciliation, and incident response practices. Drive operational excellence for business-critical financial workflows.

  • Customer Experience & Transparency: Champion a customer-first approach to billing by improving clarity and usability of billing surfaces, APIs, and cost insights. Partner with product and design to simplify complex billing concepts, ensuring customers can easily understand, predict, and trust their usage and costs.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Operate effectively across a wide range of stakeholders by partnering closely with Product, Finance, Legal, and Go-To-Market teams. Balance competing technical, financial, regulatory, and customer requirements while driving alignment and execution across multiple organizations.

  • Team Building & Execution: Build and lead a high-performing engineering team by hiring, mentoring, and developing engineers across levels. Foster a strong team culture focused on ownership, quality, and impact, driving execution against ambitious goals in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • People Management & Team Leadership Demonstrate strong people management and team leadership with 2–3 years of experience managing engineering teams. Bring a track record of delivering impactful projects through others, with experience coaching and developing engineers.

  • Technical Acumen Bring strong backend and distributed systems fundamentals, with experience building or operating reliable, scalable systems. Guide architecture and make sound technical tradeoffs with a deep understanding of data integrity and correctness in high-stakes systems.

  • Operational Excellence Value reliability and precision in critical systems, with experience in monitoring, alerting, and incident management. Bring an appreciation for correctness, auditability, and long-term maintainability, with comfort operating systems where accuracy is non-negotiable.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration Exhibit excellent technical communication skills, both verbal and written, to effectively collaborate across diverse roles and functions. As this team will have customers across the engineering organization, this role requires the ability to field multiple requests from multiple teams while still fulfilling a unified mission.

  • Organizational Prowess Be extremely organized, capable of managing complex initiatives and team priorities effectively.

  • Required Education Bachelor's degree minimum.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with billing, payments, or financial systems

  • Familiarity with usage-based pricing models or cloud platforms

  • Experience working in highly regulated or high-accuracy domains

  • Passion for building systems that directly impact customer trust

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

Crusoe's mission is to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. We’re crafting the engine that powers a world where people can create ambitiously with AI — without sacrificing scale, speed, or sustainability.

Be a part of the AI revolution with sustainable technology at Crusoe. Here, you'll drive meaningful innovation, make a tangible impact, and join a team that’s setting the pace for responsible, transformative cloud infrastructure.

About the Role: As the Senior Staff Engineer for Data Center Operations, you are the technical architect and strategic "right hand" to the Director of Data Center Operations. You will bridge the gap between high-level hardware engineering and ground-level execution, ensuring our AI fleet—from our current H200 and Blackwell (GB200) clusters to upcoming GB300 and Rubin architectures—is the most reliable and maintainable in the world. This is a high-impact role focused on operational maturity, technical governance, and the systems that power our global white space.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Operational Governance & Metrics: Oversee the technical health of our global ticket queue. Partner with internal teams to develop real-time dashboards and track the KPIs/SLAs (MTTR, fleet availability, sparing accuracy) that measure our operational maturity.

  • Fleet Supportability & Tooling: Partner with the Fleet Engineering team to define the software access, diagnostic hooks, and physical tooling required for maximum repair efficiency. Act as the primary advocate for "serviceability" within the white space.

  • Power Topology Strategy: Lead the initiative to map end-to-end "Power Strings," from main distribution down to cabinet PDUs. Lead the Build vs. Buy analysis to determine whether we develop internal mapping tools or procure a third-party solution.

  • Operational Resilience: Architect the framework for our Business Continuity (BCP) and Disaster Recovery (DR) plans. Define the technical protocols for hardware recovery and site-level failovers to ensure minimal disruption to our AI Cloud customers.

  • Technical Advisory & Documentation: Provide expert guidance and architectural "sign-off" to the internal Documentation Committee. Ensure all break-fix SOPs and technical playbooks are accurate, safe, and optimized for global scale.

  • Advanced Escalation & Mentorship: Serve as the final technical authority for systemic or complex hardware failures. Mentor senior technicians and site leads, elevating the collective technical IQ of the global operations team.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Technical Mastery: 10+ years in Data Center Operations, Systems Engineering, or HPC hardware, with an expert-level understanding of x86/GPU server architecture and electrical distribution.

  • The "Supportability" Mindset: Proven experience in hardware maintenance at scale. You know how to translate field challenges into technical requirements for Engineering and Fleet teams to minimize downtime.

  • Hardware Expertise: Deep familiarity with high-density AI infrastructure, including current NVIDIA H200 and Blackwell (GB200) systems, with the ability to architect support strategies for the transition to GB300 and Rubin platforms.

  • Data-Driven Leadership: Expert proficiency in defining operational KPIs and building dashboards (e.g., Tableau, Grafana) to drive "Operational Maturity."

  • Strategic Decision Making: Experience performing Build vs. Buy analyses for technical tools and infrastructure software, justifying decisions with clear ROI and technical requirements.

  • Communication: Exceptional ability to distill complex technical risks, ticket-queue trends, and infrastructure hurdles into clear, actionable strategies for senior leadership.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $179,000 -$218,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

The Marketing Events Manager will be a key driver in scaling our event marketing programs, focusing on operational excellence and high-impact execution. This role is ideal for a highly organized and structured events professional with a successful track record of delivering high-volume proprietary (1P) and third-party (3P) events. You will be responsible for end-to-end event management, ensuring seamless execution, measurable results, and strong cross-functional partnerships to support our rapid growth.

Key to success is your ability to quickly establish repeatable, scalable event processes. You will take a customer-focused and programmatic approach to designing and executing events that drive value. It is essential that you are knowledgeable and engaged with Crusoe’s mission and products to ensure our execution drives the desired business outcomes.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Design, plan, and execute a diverse portfolio of events, including large-scale industry trade shows, bespoke high-touch sales events, and technical thought leadership meetups.

  • Establish scalable event processes, templates, and best practices to ensure repeatable, high-quality execution as the company and event volume grow.

  • Develop and manage comprehensive event project plans, timelines, and budgets, ensuring all operational milestones are met.

  • Serve as the primary program manager, driving cross-functional alignment and accountability across sales, marketing, product, dev rel, and leadership teams to orchestrate cohesive events.

  • Oversee all event logistics and operations, including venue sourcing, vendor management, contract negotiation, registration, booth/set design, staffing, and post-event reporting and lead follow-up.

  • Manage vendor relationships (agencies, production, catering, etc.), ensuring high-quality service and cost efficiency.

  • Develop and maintain detailed event performance metrics and reports, analyzing ROI and proposing improvements for future events.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 7-10 years of experience in event marketing, marketing operations, or program management, preferably within a high-growth high-tech environment.

  • Proven track record of managing and executing complex events, including large tradeshows and high-touch executive programs.

  • Exceptional organizational, project management, and attention-to-detail skills, with a structured approach to problem-solving.

  • Strong understanding of event logistics, contract negotiation, vendor management, and budget administration.

  • Strong program management capabilities, including the ability to influence and drive alignment among diverse cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., sales, marketing, legal).

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable interacting with internal executives and external partners.

  • Proficiency with event management software (e.g., Cvent, Splash) and CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce).

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $159,000- $193,000 Base + Annual Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

The Executive Assistant (EA) will be responsible for supporting the Chief Real Estate Officer and Senior Vice President of Real Estate, helping drive operational effectiveness for Crusoe’s rapidly expanding commercial real estate and data center development organization. This role requires a dynamic, highly adaptable professional who can flex their approach based on the needs of each executive while operating with discretion, sound judgment, and a strong sense of ownership.

The EA will proactively anticipate needs, manage competing priorities, and ensure the smooth coordination of calendars, travel, and key business activities across multiple locations. Given the pace and scale of Crusoe’s real estate growth, this role requires someone who thrives in a fast-moving environment and can support leaders navigating complex development timelines, cross-functional coordination, and external stakeholder engagement.

As the Executive Assistant, you will be required to work on-site five days per week. You will collaborate closely with other Executive Assistants, Workplace Managers, and cross-functional partners. Responsibilities may evolve as the company continues to scale. By ensuring operational efficiency and strong executive coordination, you will contribute directly to Crusoe’s mission of accelerating the abundance of energy and intelligence.

This is a full-time, in-office position based in San Francisco.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Manage executive inboxes with a high degree of care and judgment — triaging, drafting responses, flagging urgent items, and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks, even when the executive isn't actively engaged.

  • Provide high-quality, timely, and detail-oriented administrative support to Crusoe’s Real Estate leadership, including managing complex calendars, preparing confidential correspondence, arranging travel, processing expenses, and ensuring stakeholders are informed and aligned.

  • Coordinate and manage executive calendars across multiple time zones, balancing internal leadership meetings, cross-functional collaboration, and external engagements with brokers, partners, and vendors.

  • Support coordination for the Real Estate leadership team and their direct reports to ensure alignment across development projects, portfolio planning, and strategic initiatives.

  • Thoughtfully manage scheduling requests to maximize executive effectiveness and protect focus time while ensuring key priorities move forward.

  • Improve meeting effectiveness by preparing agendas, gathering context and materials, capturing notes, tracking decisions and action items, and ensuring follow-through.

  • Assist with planning and execution of leadership offsites, project reviews, team events, and strategic planning sessions, including logistics, vendor coordination, agenda development, and on-site support.

  • Partner closely with other Executive Assistants, Workplace Managers, and cross-functional teams to coordinate travel, conferences, site visits, and company events.

  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve communication, and strengthen operational coordination across the Real Estate team.
    Support occasional personal tasks or administrative needs for leadership as required.

  • Maintain accessibility during the traditional work week, with occasional flexibility outside standard hours when urgent business needs arise.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • You have 5-7 years of experience in an executive administrative role.

  • You have a background in real estate, acquisitions, or development — or have directly supported executives in these fields — and can engage fluently with deal flow, site timelines, and portfolio language.

  • Experience working with and supporting technology/software teams is desirable.

  • You have exceptional communication skills—written, verbal, and interpersonal.

  • You possess strong attention to detail—accuracy in numbers, logistics, and communication.

  • You exercise discretion and confidentiality with sensitive information.

  • You can prioritize conflicting needs and manage time effectively in a fast-paced environment.

  • You have proven success in planning and executing team offsites or large-scale events.

  • You have experience helping an executive learn how to work with an EA — you know how to build trust, create structure for delegation, and establish workflows that make the partnership more effective over time

  • You are proactive, always looking for ways to help and improve processes.

  • You can operate with minimal direction. You piece together context from limited information, take initiative, and move work forward without waiting to be told what to do.

  • You can work independently while keeping stakeholders informed and aligned.

  • You are proficient in Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, Slides, etc.).

  • You can prioritize conflicting needs and manage time effectively in a fast-paced environment.

  • You are eager to grow with the organization and take on new challenges.

  • You embody the company values and contribute positively to Crusoe’s culture

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $104,000 - $126,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Manager, Strategic Initiatives - Innovation
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI infrastructure company with a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. We design and build our own data centers, manufacture critical infrastructure components, and operate our cloud platform. Our unique position — spanning power, manufacturing, infrastructure, compute, and AI services — gives us the ability to move faster and differentiate in ways that horizontally organized competitors cannot.

The Strategy team exists to turn that structural advantage into action. We develop, evaluate, and drive strategic initiatives that align with Crusoe’s mission and compound our differentiation over time. You will be a Manager on this team, responsible for screening new opportunities, leading in-depth evaluations, and driving cross-functional work to bring the strongest concepts to life. This is not a support role. You will own initiatives end-to-end, present findings directly to the C-suite, and shape where this company invests its capital and attention.

Your Mission:

Turn ambiguity into conviction. Your job is to take emerging market signals, inbound partnership pitches, and early-stage concepts and produce clear, defensible recommendations that the most senior people at Crusoe can act on. You will do this by pulling on domain expertise from business units, R&D, corporate functions, and external experts then synthesizing it into a point of view that enables quality decisions and thoughtful risk management.

This role blends strategic analysis with operational execution. Some opportunities will require deep analytical work; others will require you to lead a cross-functional group to develop a concept, manage workstreams, and test hypotheses. You should be equally comfortable building a financial model and running a kickoff meeting.

Over time, you will develop a thematic specialization based on your background and the evolving needs of the business. Regardless of lane, you will be expected to operate across the full Crusoe stack and maintain fluency in all of it.

What You'll Be Working On:

Opportunity Screening

  • Lead initial strategic fit assessments for new opportunities, determining whether they warrant deeper investment of team time and resources.

  • Produce written recommendations with clear reasoning for advancing or declining opportunities.

  • Build and maintain the institutional record of evaluated opportunities so that Crusoe learns from every decision.

Strategic Evaluation & Cross-Functional Execution

  • Own full evaluation cycles for assigned initiatives: market sizing, financial modeling, competitive landscape analysis, risk assessment, and strategic fit.

  • Lead cross-functional working groups to develop concepts that require input and coordination across multiple business units. Drive the process from early scoping through executive decision and integration.

  • Produce robust, fact-based whitepapers that stand on their own as decision documents for senior leadership.

  • Coordinate with executive sponsors and pull structured inputs from teams across the organization without creating deliverable burden on those teams.

Relationship Management & Organizational Navigation

  • Build strong, trust-based relationships across Crusoe’s divisions — engineering, manufacturing, infrastructure, product, energy, finance, and corporate development — so that you know who to ask what question and have the credibility to get high engagement when you do.

  • Invest in understanding each team’s priorities, constraints, and expertise so that your outreach adds value rather than creating work.

  • Socialize strategic concepts with Directors and VPs across business units, building organizational context and alignment ahead of executive decisions.

Market Intelligence & Strategic Context

  • Stay current on market trends, emerging technologies, competitive dynamics, and developments in the AI infrastructure landscape to ensure the team’s evaluations are grounded in the latest context.

  • Proactively surface opportunities and risks based on your market awareness, not just evaluate what comes inbound.

  • Drive strategic insights and develop theories of investment (internal and external) by translating Crusoe’s strategy into operational deliverables.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Professional Background

  • 5–8 years of experience in management consulting, corporate development, venture capital, or strategy at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company.

  • Demonstrated experience producing executive-level written deliverables: investment memos, board materials, strategic recommendations with financial backing.

  • Track record of independently owning complex, multi-stakeholder analytical projects with senior leadership as the audience.

  • Experience leading cross-functional workstreams — not just contributing to them. You have been the person responsible for driving an initiative across teams with competing priorities.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous environments where the scope, process, and answer are not predefined. You have built the path, not just walked it.

  • Evidence of building productive stakeholder relationships across organizational boundaries, particularly with technical, operational, and commercial teams.

  • Domain exposure to one or more of the following: data center infrastructure, energy and power markets, AI products and computing.

Behavioral Traits

  • Ownership Mentality: You take full accountability for your work and your recommendations. When you own an initiative, you own it completely — the analysis, the stakeholder coordination, the recommendation, and the outcome.

  • Executive Presence: You are credible and composed in front of Directors and VPs. You can hold a room and drive a productive discussion under pressure.

  • Speed with Rigor: You default to action and produce high-quality work on compressed timelines.

  • Organizational Fluency: You navigate cross-functional complexity without creating friction. You pull on teams by adding value, not by creating work.

  • Intellectual Curiosity: You are energized by learning how a data center actually works, how power is traded, or how infrastructure scales.

What You Get:

  • Direct exposure to C-suite decision-making on Crusoe’s most consequential strategic bets.

  • A front-row seat to the intersection of AI, energy, and infrastructure at one of the fastest-growing companies in the space.

  • The intellectual variety of a new strategic challenge every cycle, spanning energy, cloud architecture, partnerships, and competitive strategy.

  • A team that values ownership and gives you the autonomy to run with your work.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $140,250 - $170,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is on a mission to align the future of computing with the future of the climate. We provide a reliable, scalable, and environmentally friendly solution for AI infrastructure by harnessing large-scale clean energy and building AI-optimized data centers. As the industry’s first vertically integrated AI infrastructure provider, we empower builders to reach their AI potential responsibly.

Reporting to the Senior Manager of Indirect Tax, you will play a key role in the accounting team assisting with indirect tax compliance, planning, and strategy. This is a high-impact position that sits at the intersection of tax technology and climate-friendly infrastructure, helping Crusoe navigate complex tax landscapes as we scale our global footprint.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Compliance Management: Assist with indirect tax compliance across multiple domains, including Sales and Use tax, VAT, and Property tax.

  • Research & Incentives: Research and prepare indirect tax incentives and credits for various jurisdictions and large-scale projects.

  • Audit Defense: Support indirect tax audits and manage refund claims to ensure financial accuracy and recovery.

  • Transaction Support: Assist with mergers and acquisitions (M&A) and various strategic transactions as needed.

  • Tax Technology Transformation: Play a pivotal role in technology projects, including establishing tax-related software requirements, testing, and documentation.

  • Strategic Projects: Support ad-hoc tasks and special projects as requested by the Senior Manager to drive department efficiency.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting; a Master’s in Accounting or Tax is highly preferred.

  • Experience: 3–5 years of indirect tax experience within a large public accounting firm or corporate organization. Experience in the construction or technology industries is a significant advantage.

  • Licensure: CPA license (or actively seeking a CPA license) is preferred.

  • Technical Proficiency: Keen attention to detail with high comfort levels in tax software and advanced Microsoft Excel functions.

  • Professional Attributes: A self-starter with a natural curiosity to learn different types of tax and the motivation to drive process improvements in a fast-paced environment.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with automated tax engines (e.g., Vertex, Avalara, or OneSource).

  • Prior exposure to international VAT/GST requirements for cloud or digital services.

  • Experience with ERP implementation and tax-sensitization of financial data.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Workplace Manager to help get our new Brighton location off the ground. This is a unique opportunity to play a foundational role in establishing a high-functioning environment from day one. You will be instrumental in creating a professional, welcoming space for the Brighton team, directly shaping a productive culture as the site grows.

Partnering with the Senior Workplace Manager, you will manage daily operations, site-specific projects, and employee engagement initiatives. The ideal candidate has 4+ years of experience in workplace coordination or operations and thrives in the "build" phase of a new office.

This is an in-office position based in Brighton, CO, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Site Launch & Operations: Take ownership of the Brighton office functionality. Conduct regular checks to ensure workspaces, conference rooms, and shared areas are clean, well-stocked, and fully operational.

  • Internal Office Construction & Setup: Manage internal updates to the new space, including furniture installation, office remodels, and interior design changes to align with Crusoe standards.

  • Workplace Enhancement: Proactively identify needs for the new location, creating a dynamic and inclusive environment that reflects Crusoe’s values from the start.

  • Event & Team Support: Assist in planning and executing site-specific events, including setup, teardown, and catering coordination for local team milestones.

  • Employee Engagement: Foster a positive workplace culture by supporting local engagement initiatives and team-building activities tailored to the Brighton crew.

  • Vendor Management: Identify and manage local vendors (cleaning, maintenance, snacks, etc.) that contribute to a seamless employee experience.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work across departments to gather feedback on the new space and identify opportunities to elevate the day-to-day experience.

  • Facility Readiness: Coordinate the daily setup of the workspace, ensuring visiting team members have a seamless, "plug-and-play" experience when working out of the Brighton office.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Workplace Coordination Experience: 4+ years of experience in workplace coordination or operational roles, ideally within fast-paced, growth-oriented organizations.

  • Site Setup Mentality: A proven ability to manage the "blank canvas" of a new office, from supply chain management to furniture logistics.

  • Organizational Excellence: Exceptional organizational skills with a keen eye for detail, prioritization, and the ability to multitask in a developing environment.

  • Problem-Solving Skills: A creative problem-solver who brings fresh ideas to improve operational efficiency and solve the unique challenges of a new location.

  • Collaboration Skills: Ability to work effectively with remote leadership and local teams to ensure Brighton operations run smoothly.

  • Logistics Expertise: Experience maintaining a functional, safe, and well-organized office environment.

  • Passion for Experience: A genuine drive to create engaging, top-tier workplace environments that people are excited to walk into every morning.

  • Experience with visitor management systems.

  • Experience in a fast-growing tech company.

  • Event planning experience.

About This Role:

This is a high-impact opportunity as the first dedicated Accounting & Finance hire, offering significant ownership and exposure across the entire business. As the Senior Manager of General Ledger will be the foundational leader of our financial operations, responsible for building the systems, processes, and team that will support Crusoe's rapid scaling.

As a key strategic partner to leadership, you will move beyond standard accounting to architect a modern, AI-enabled finance stack. The ideal candidate is a technical expert with a "builder mindset" who thrives in fast-evolving environments and is comfortable creating internal controls and reporting structures from the ground up.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Corporate Accounting Ownership: Own key corporate accounting areas, including expense accruals, equity compensation, debt, and complex balance sheet and P&L accounts.

  • Technical SME: Act as the subject matter expert for complex technical issues, including leases, capitalization, financing, business combinations, segments, and foreign currency.

  • Close Management: Manage the monthly and quarterly close process, ensuring accurate and timely results in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

  • Process Automation: Drive process improvements and automation initiatives to enhance scalability and close efficiency using modern finance tools.

  • Internal Controls & SOX: Ensure strong internal controls over financial reporting, including control design, documentation, and remediation of deficiencies.

  • Audit Leadership: Serve as the primary point of contact for external and internal auditors, managing the relationship and ensuring audit readiness.

  • Team Development: Lead and develop a team of corporate accounting professionals, providing oversight, coaching, and performance management.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education & Licensure: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting and a CPA are required.

  • Experience: 8+ years of prior work experience; public accounting experience is highly preferred.

  • Technical Mastery: In-depth knowledge of U.S. GAAP and extensive experience in technical accounting and financial reporting.

  • Analytical Rigor: Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with a high level of proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

  • Builder Mindset: Proven success in creating efficiencies, systems, and controls in a fast-paced, autonomous environment.

  • Industry Context: Experience with complex legal/reporting structures; real estate or data center industry experience is a significant plus.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Direct experience implementing or managing modern finance stacks and AI-enabled accounting tools.

  • Experience navigating the transition from a private to a public company reporting environment.

  • Familiarity with international accounting standards and multi-currency consolidations.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $132,000 -$160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to drive the systems, data, and processes that power our go-to-market engine. This high impact role is ideal for someone who loves building scalable systems, digging into data, and removing friction across the revenue cycle. A core focus will be owning sales compensation operations and leading the eventual implementation of a commission automation platform, but this role is broader: you'll be a key architect of how our revenue team operates and scales.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Own the end-to-end monthly commission calculation process for all quota-carrying roles, ensuring accuracy and on-time payout.

  • Maintain commission plan documentation, policies, and rep-facing resources.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for commission inquiries, disputes, and exception handling.

  • Partners cross functionally to reconcile payouts and support compensation-related audits and reporting.

  • Identify manual, inefficient workflows in the compensation and RevOps stack and build scalable solutions.

  • Build and maintain Salesforce reports, dashboards, and workflows that support commission tracking and sales performance visibility.

  • Leverage Excel and Google Sheets to model comp plans, run scenario analysis, and bridge gaps ahead of full tooling implementation.

  • Document processes to create a repeatable, audit-ready compensation operation.

  • Lead the evaluation, selection, and implementation of a commission automation platform (e.g., CaptivateIQ, Spiff, Xactly), including requirements definition, vendor management, Salesforce integration, and end-user rollout.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 4-7 years of experience in Revenue Operations focusing on process improvement and incentive compensation administration, preferably within a high growth, B2B technology environment.

  • Hands-on experience running commission operations meaning you've owned the process, not just supported it

  • Strong Salesforce proficiency (reporting, dashboards, data hygiene)

  • Advanced Excel and/or Google Sheets skills (complex formulas, pivot tables, modeling)

  • High attention to detail and comfort working with large, messy datasets

  • Strong communication skills — able to explain comp mechanics clearly to reps and executives alike

  • Experience implementing a commission automation tool (CaptivateIQ, Spiff, Xactly, Commissionly, or similar)

  • Familiarity with technology industry sales compensation structures (ARR-based quotas, accelerators, SPIFs, etc.)

  • Experience at a growth-stage company where you've had to build or rebuild processes from scratch

Bonus Points

  • Experience with hyperscalers, GPU clouds, or high-performance compute environments.

  • Familiarity with large-scale AI training and inference architectures.

  • Strong network in the AI/ML and enterprise technology ecosystem.

  • Track record of working with Fortune 500 enterprises and digitally native businesses on transformative infrastructure deals.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $136,000 - $165,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

Join our team as a Field Acceptance Testing Technician, where you'll play a crucial role in ensuring the quality and compliance of our electrical products. You'll be responsible for conducting thorough inspections and tests on electrical components, subassemblies, and finished goods, ranging from intricate control cabinets to large-scale modular buildings. Your attention to detail and expertise will directly impact our ability to deliver high-quality, safe, and reliable products to our customers. This position requires a detail-oriented individual with a strong electrical background and a commitment to maintaining rigorous quality standards. This is a full-time position. (#INDMFG)

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Electrical Inspections: Conduct ongoing inspections of all electrical installations, subassemblies, and finished goods to ensure compliance with standards.

  • Process Audits: Execute audits of electrical assembly, control wiring, power distribution wiring, and commercial wiring installation processes.

  • Testing and Reporting: Assist in or prepare testing and commissioning reports to document product performance and compliance.

  • Quality Standards Documentation: Document quality standards and specifications related to electrical installations and assembly, and collaborate on training.

  • Compliance Verification: Ensure all work is executed per approved standards and drawings, identifying and addressing deviations.

  • Non-Conformance Documentation: Document material non-conformances found during inspections of work in process, finished goods, and receiving.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with safety, engineering, and manufacturing teams to improve design for manufacturing and reduce inefficiencies.

  • Regulatory Compliance: Ensure product designs comply with regulatory, commercial code, customer specifications, and engineering standards.

  • Tool Calibration: Assist with the execution of the tool calibration program, focusing on electrical test equipment.

  • Additional Duties: Perform other job duties as assigned to support the quality assurance process.

  • Travel 80% of the time to job sites where Crusoe Industries products have been deployed. When not traveling, support Crusoe Industries production teams at our Brighton, Colorado manufacturing site.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Journeyman Electrician Preferred

  • Detail Orientation: Must be detail-driven with a strong focus on accuracy and quality.

  • Communication Skills: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills for effective collaboration.

  • Analytical and Decision-Making: High-level analytical ability and sound decision-making skills.

  • Physical Requirements: Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and stand, walk, stoop, and bend for extended periods.

  • Electrical Experience: Journeyman Electrician with 5+ years of industry experience or 7+ years in electrical assembly/inspection.

  • Electrical Systems Knowledge: Previous exposure to low and medium voltage electrical installations.

  • Standards Knowledge: Working knowledge of IEC, NEC, NFPA, IEEE, and NETA testing specifications.

  • Technical Knowledge: Working knowledge of Programmable Logic Controllers, VFDs, HMI, MCC, and UPS.

  • Component Identification: Ability to identify electrical components, hardware, and equipment.

  • Schematic Interpretation: Ability to read, understand, and trace electrical schematics.

  • Computer Skills: Basic computer skills with Word/Excel experience; scheduling software knowledge is a plus.

  • Safety and Compliance: Must pass background check and drug/alcohol testing due to safety-sensitive position.

  • Travel: Up to 100% travel depending on project needs, including overnight stays.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with lean manufacturing and 5S methodologies.

  • Experience with ISO 9001 quality management systems.

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification.

  • Knowledge of Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems, particularly Accumatica ERP.

  • Experience with advanced project management methodologies.

  • Previous experience improving project workflows.

  • Advanced knowledge of manufacturing processes.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $33 -$36/HR + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

Site Selection Engineer

Location: San Francisco, CA (Required 5 days/week) Reports To: Sr. Manager, Site Selection

Position Overview

Crusoe is seeking a Site Selection Engineer to lead the technical and commercial evaluation of our global data center expansion. This is not a traditional analyst role; you will serve as the primary bridge between our high-density GPU engineering requirements and the global colocation market. You will own the "deal lifecycle"—from initial site identification and technical due diligence to the negotiation of complex leases and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

The ideal candidate possesses the "binary" lens required for technical engineering validation and the "artful" lens required for high-stakes commercial negotiations. You will ensure that every megawatt we lease is technically capable of supporting Blackwell-class GPU clusters and commercially structured to protect Crusoe’s long-term interests.

What You’ll Be Working On

Deal Execution & Lease Negotiation:

  • Lead Commercial Negotiations: Drive the execution of Letters of Intent (LOIs) and definitive Leases (Master Lease Agreements/Service Orders). Negotiate power ramp schedules, expansion options, termination rights, and holdover clauses.

  • SLA Development: Author and negotiate rigorous Service Level Agreements. Define critical parameters for uptime, temperature/humidity envelopes (including liquid cooling/DLC requirements), PUE guarantees, and liquidated damages for delivery delays.

  • TCO Modeling: Build comprehensive Total Cost of Ownership models that account for base rent, metered power, PUE premiums, operating expenses, and local tax abatements (e.g., Texas HB 1223).

Technical Due Diligence & Engineering Oversight:

  • Infrastructure Validation: Perform deep-dive technical due diligence on provider sites. Review one-line diagrams, P&IDs, and floor plans to verify redundancy levels (N+1/2N), fiber latency, and structural floor loading.

  • High-Density Strategy: Assess provider readiness for high-density GPU deployments (50kW–1,000kW+ per rack), including cooling loop capacities, water availability for RDHx/DLC, and power busway limits.

  • Schedule & Risk Analysis: Audit provider construction schedules and commissioning plans (L1–L5). Identify potential "hard-down" risks and supply chain bottlenecks that could impact RFS (Ready for Service) dates.

Strategic Site Selection:

  • Market Intelligence: Identify and track global capacity "pockets" with low-cost/renewable energy access and optimal fiber connectivity.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner with Legal, Construction, Cloud TPMs, and Finance to ensure site selections align with Crusoe’s rapidly evolving product roadmap.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

  • Experience: 3–7 years in Data Center Site Selection, Infrastructure Strategy, or Data Center Engineering/Development.

  • Technical Literacy: Ability to interpret electrical/mechanical engineering drawings and translate technical constraints into commercial lease protections.

  • Negotiation Grit: Proven track record of redlining SLAs and negotiating business terms with Tier-1 colocation providers (Equinix, Digital Realty, Vantage, etc.).

  • Financial Mastery: Advanced financial modeling skills in Excel; ability to structure complex "buy vs. lease" and "CAPEX vs. OPEX" scenarios.

  • Market Knowledge: Deep understanding of data center power structures (Gross vs. NNN), utility interconnection processes, and regional tax incentive programs.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical/Mechanical), Finance, or Real Estate.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $155,000 -$188,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
